# Follow-up repository audit — 2026-09-23

Baseline: `718bedbb59cc3925b5a226caf7c468b82d932867`. Scope: repository setup, publication/ownership controls, indexing, file discoverability and licensing consistency. This is not independent replication of the research experiment or a guarantee of perpetual availability/security.

## Observed baseline

The public repository has an active main ruleset, required `ori-validation`, zero required human reviews, administrator bypass and enabled repository auto-merge. CC0-1.0 is recognized by GitHub. Latest inspected scheduled publisher run 35833248521 succeeded. The old duplicate index PRs are closed.

Physical inventory: **1 published Idea, 24 files, 4 Markdown documents, 6 SVGs and 9 CSV files**. The earlier audit comment's 23-file count was an off-by-one reporting error; this audit counts all six figures. All four Markdown texts and Git blob hashes match the existing machine catalog. 38 repository-relative Markdown links resolved. SVG XML, CSV structure and Python syntax were checked without executing the research program.

## Regression-first findings

The original 56 tests still passed. A first batch of 14 additional edge tests ran against the unchanged implementation: 12 failed. These failures exposed missing boundary guards, not a claim that an external attacker actually exploited the repository. They covered:

- aggregate Markdown size could pass the access validator and then fail indexing after merge;
- cached reads did not reapply a smaller requested byte limit;
- creation time parsing accepted missing seconds;
- a checked license example inside fenced code/comments or outside an Issue's Declaration could be misinterpreted as consent;
- duplicate form headings and multiline titles were ambiguous;
- a retargeted PR was not rechecked against `main`, and draft state was not rechecked by the publisher before attempting merge (GitHub itself also enforces draft restrictions).

## Changes

- Enforce the same byte limits before merge and during indexing, including unchanged Markdown in a touched Idea.
- Build the complete virtual catalog before merging an ordinary contributor PR. Explicitly cap the machine index at 64 MiB; reject rather than silently omit data.
- Mask code/comments before parsing form fields or consent; preserve original Markdown for publication and full-text indexing. Require a unique set of form headings and one-line title.
- Recheck live PR state, head, target branch, consent body and author before merge.
- Isolate input/PR resolution failures; do not hide global service/authentication errors.
- Avoid unbounded regex backtracking on malformed link/HTML markers in plaintext extraction.
- Separate `Data` and `Results` links when both directories exist.
- Both workflows discover all test files rather than running only the original test module.
- Remove the temporary source-export steps used for this audit before merging.

**81 tests pass locally**: the original 56 plus 25 additional regression/preflight tests. A local source snapshot was obtained through a temporary read-only GitHub artifact because the analysis container cannot connect directly to GitHub; baseline script SHA values were checked against the actual Git blobs before testing.

## Unchanged guarantees and boundaries

- UI remains the same small root with `ideas/` and `.github/`; at least one nonempty Markdown file is still sufficient.
- Existing ID, creation time, CC0 license and research results are not changed by this infrastructure patch.
- Search classification remains rule-based, not an LLM service or novelty certificate. Local catalog coverage does not force external search engines/AI services to index a page.
- Contribution and reuse permissions remain separate. CC0 does not override third-party rights, patents/trademarks or non-waivable rights.
- The metadata description expresses a research-workflow vision; the hosted Actions perform repository operations, not autonomous experiments.
- The research package still has documented reproduction gaps in `reproducibility/RUN.md`. This audit does not fabricate or rerun those missing scientific outputs.
- GitHub API limits, event delays, schedule suspension and administrator actions remain operational boundaries. No paid service, external token or weakened branch rule was introduced.

Production run IDs and merge results are recorded in the audit PR after verification, rather than predicted here.
